title: Only 11% Can Pass This Firefighter Entrance Exam
summary: Fire science, tools, hazards and fast incident decisions test how clearly you think under pressure.

landing.intro: Fire behaviour, hazard spotting, mechanical reasoning and split-second judgement. Can you stay calm when every clue matters?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge uses ten carefully varied questions to explore entrance-level firefighter reasoning. It covers fire and smoke science, scene hazards, equipment mechanics, practical numeracy, spatial awareness, clear communication and incident judgement.

The challenge moves quickly from accessible foundations into changing conditions, practical mechanics and integrated incident decisions. Questions use worldwide-safe principles rather than local ranks, codes, building rules or operational firefighting procedures.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the entrance areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of operational readiness or suitability for firefighter employment.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Work through all ten questions at your own pace; there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose the single option best supported by the visible clues. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal.
Finish the challenge to reveal your score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited firefighter entrance exam, employment assessment, fitness test, qualification, operational training course or source of emergency advice. Fire-service procedures vary worldwide; always follow local emergency services and qualified professional guidance.

checkpoint.finalAdNote: One short ad, then your results.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your firefighter score and five-area breakdown are ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Entrance Exam Standout
profile-1.copy: You combined excellent fire-science foundations with calm, evidence-led judgement across the entire challenge. Changing hazards, mechanical clues and communication details stayed clear even when the final decisions became demanding.

profile-2.title: The Sharp Incident Thinker
profile-2.copy: You showed a strong feel for the science, mechanics and safety reasoning behind the challenge. Most of the hazard, calculation and prioritisation traps did not pull you off course.

profile-3.title: The Calm Incident Solver
profile-3.copy: You handled a broad mix of fire behaviour, practical mechanics and multi-clue decisions with steady reasoning. A few finer observation and communication details kept the challenge interesting.

profile-4.title: The Steady Crew Candidate
profile-4.copy: You built a solid result by following visible evidence and treating safety seriously. Your strongest area shows where your entrance-exam thinking became most assured.

profile-5.title: The Promising Recruit
profile-5.copy: You solved a good share of the challenge and showed useful instincts across several entrance areas. The answer review will reveal which foundations are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The First-Alarm Explorer
profile-6.copy: The challenge uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, safety-first judgement. Every reviewed answer is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind calm incident thinking.

firefighter-s1q1.question: Heat and fuel are present. Which third element is needed to complete the fire triangle?

firefighter-s1q2.question: A sparking electrical panel stands beside a pool of water. What is the safest first response?
answers: Step through the water to switch it off
Pour more water over the panel
Move the panel by its outer case
Keep people clear and alert qualified responders

visual.ariaLabel: Earlier smoke was light and steady, but it is now increasing rapidly

firefighter-s2q2.question: Which report best communicates the change without guessing at its cause?
answers: Smoke at the north doorway has changed from light and steady to rapidly increasing
The exact burning material has been identified from the smoke
Nothing important has changed because smoke was already present
The fire will definitely remain in the same area

firefighter-s1q5.question: A pry bar is used as a lever. What usually happens when the grip moves farther from the pivot?
answers: Less force is needed for the same turning effect

firefighter-s3q6.question: A hot surface warms your face from several metres away without contact. Which heat-transfer process best explains this?

visual.ariaLabel: A map scale of one centimetre to twelve point five metres and a route measuring four point eight centimetres

firefighter-s3q2.question: What real distance does the route represent?

firefighter-s4q7.question: A fire-damaged roof is sagging and fresh cracks are appearing. What is the safest interpretation?
answers: The cracks show exactly where to stand
Collapse is possible, so keep clear and report the changing condition
The damage matters only after the incident

visual.ariaLabel: Clockwise Gear A drives Gear B, which drives Gear C

firefighter-s5q5.question: Gear A drives B, and B drives C. Which way does Gear C turn?
answers: It cannot turn because three gears are used
Upward because Gear A is first

visual.ariaLabel: Four crews need three lamps each, two spare lamps are required and two lamps have already been issued

firefighter-s5q6.question: How many more lamps must be drawn so every crew is equipped and two spares remain?

visual.ariaLabel: Smoke is thickening in the west corridor, two people are unaccounted for, the east exit is clear and a routine equipment count is due

firefighter-s5q8.question: What is the best first action and report?
answers: Finish the count before reporting the smoke
Direct people east; report west smoke and two missing people; defer the count
Use the west corridor because it is shortest
